en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us; (H) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: 'Abdah and Abu Usamah narrated to us—all of them from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). And in the hadith of Ibn Bishr and 'Abdah: "No one will narrate it to you after me; I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say..." and he mentioned the like of it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: I heard Qatadah narrating from Anas ibn Malik that he said: Shall I not narrate to you a hadith which I heard from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and which no one after me who heard it from him will narrate to you? "Indeed, among the portents of the Hour are that knowledge will be taken away, ignorance will become prevalent, fornication will become rampant, intoxicants will be drunk, men will depart, and women will remain, until there is one keeper for fifty women."

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us: Abu al-Tayyah narrated to us: Anas ibn Malik narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Among the portents of the Hour are that knowledge will be taken away, ignorance will take hold, intoxicants will be drunk, and fornication will become prevalent."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Hafs ibn Ghiyath and Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Sulayman ibn 'Atiq, from Talq ibn Habib, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Ruined are the extremists." He said it three times.

Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Abu Ghassan narrated to us: Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, and he mentioned the hadith similarly.
And several of our companions narrated to us from Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam: Abu Ghassan—who is Muhammad ibn Mutarrif—informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to me: Hafs ibn Maysarah narrated to us: Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to me, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "You will surely follow the ways of those who were before you, handspan by handspan and arm's length by arm's length, so much so that even if they entered the hole of a lizard, you would follow them." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews and the Christians?" He said: "Who else?"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, the most hated of men to Allah is the most quarrelsome, obstinate disputant."

Ahmad ibn Sa'id ibn Sakhr al-Darimi narrated to me: Habban narrated to us: Aban narrated to us: Abu 'Imran narrated to us, saying: Jundab said to us while we were youths in Kufa: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Recite the Quran..." with the like of their hadith.

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: 'Abd al-Samad informed us: Hammam narrated to us: Abu 'Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Jundab—meaning Ibn 'Abdillah—that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Recite the Quran as long as your hearts are in harmony over it, and when you differ, then stand up (and disperse)."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu Qudamah al-Harith ibn 'Ubayd informed us, from Abu 'Imran, from Jundub ibn 'Abdillah al-Bajali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Recite the Quran as long as your hearts are in harmony over it, and when you differ over it, then stand up (and disperse)."

Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn al-Jahdari narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us: Abu 'Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Rabah al-Ansari wrote to me that 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: I went early in the heat of midday to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) one day—he said—and he heard the voices of two men disputing over a verse. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came out to us, anger visible on his face, and said: "Those who came before you were destroyed only by their differing over the Scripture."

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Yazid ibn Ibrahim al-Tustari narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) recited: {It is He who has sent down to you the Book; in it are clear verses—they are the foundation of the Book—and others are unspecific. As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they will follow that of it which is unspecific, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation. And none knows its interpretation except Allah. And those firm in knowledge say: "We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord." And none will be reminded except those of understanding.} She said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When you see those who follow what is unspecific of it, those are the ones whom Allah has named, so beware of them."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, they said: 'Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, from Rabi'ah ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and in each there is good. Strive for that which benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not feel helpless. And if anything befalls you, do not say: 'If only I had done such and such, it would have been so and so.' But rather say: 'It is the decree of Allah, and whatever He willed, He has done.' For indeed, saying 'if' opens the work of Satan."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali and Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to us—and the wording is Hajjaj's; Ishaq said: "informed us" and Hajjaj said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: al-Thawri informed us, from 'Alqamah ibn Marthad, from al-Mughirah ibn 'Abdillah al-Yashkuri, from Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: Umm Habibah said: "O Allah, grant me the enjoyment of my husband, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and of my father, Abu Sufyan, and of my brother, Mu'awiyah." So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to her: "You have asked Allah for appointed lifespans, trodden footsteps, and apportioned provisions; He will not hasten any of them before its due time, nor will He delay any of them past its due time. And had you asked Allah to grant you safety from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave, it would have been better for you." He said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, are apes and pigs among those that were transformed?" The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has never destroyed a people or punished a people and then given them descendants. Indeed, apes and pigs existed before that." Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn Ma'bad narrated it to me: al-Husayn ibn Hafs narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, with this chain of transmission, except that he said: "and reached footsteps (atharin mablughah)." Ibn Ma'bad said: And some of them narrated: "before its due time (qabla hillihi)," meaning: its arrival.

Abu Kurayb narrated it to us: Ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Mis'ar, with this chain of transmission, except that in his hadith from Ibn Bishr and Waki' together, it is: "from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Bakr's—they said: Waki' narrated to us, from Mis'ar, from 'Alqamah ibn Marthad, from al-Mughirah ibn 'Abdillah al-Yashkuri, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from 'Abdullah, who said: Umm Habibah, the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), said: "O Allah, grant me the enjoyment of my husband, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and of my father, Abu Sufyan, and of my brother, Mu'awiyah." He said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "You have asked Allah for appointed lifespans, numbered days, and apportioned provisions; He will never hasten anything before its due time or delay anything past its due time. And had you asked Allah to protect you from punishment in the Fire or punishment in the grave, it would have been better and more superior." He said: And apes were mentioned in his presence—Mis'ar said: and I think he said: and pigs—as being from transformed beings, so he said: "Indeed, Allah never made for any transformed being descendants or offspring; and apes and pigs existed before that."

Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Zakariyya narrated to us, from Talhah ibn Yahya; (H) and Sulayman ibn Ma'bad narrated to me: al-Husayn ibn Hafs narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us—both from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Talhah ibn Yahya, with Waki''s chain of transmission, the like of his hadith.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Talhah ibn Yahya, from his paternal aunt 'A'ishah bint Talhah, from 'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was invited to the funeral of a boy from the Ansar, so I said: "O Messenger of Allah, glad tidings for this one! A little sparrow from the sparrows of Paradise; he did not commit evil, nor did it reach him." He said: "Or might it be other than that, O 'A'ishah? Indeed, Allah created people for Paradise—He created them for it while they were still in the loins of their fathers; and He created people for the Fire—He created them for it while they were still in the loins of their fathers."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, from Fudayl ibn 'Amr, from 'A'ishah bint Talhah, from 'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, who said: A child died, so I said: "Glad tidings for him! A little sparrow from the sparrows of Paradise." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do you not know that Allah created Paradise and created the Fire, and He created inhabitants for this one and inhabitants for that one?"

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, from Raqabah ibn Masqalah, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, the boy whom al-Khidr killed was created a disbeliever by nature, and had he lived, he would have overwhelmed his parents with transgression and disbelief."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was asked about the children of the polytheists, so he said: "Allah knows best what they would have done when He created them."

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was asked about the children of the polytheists, whoever of them dies young, so he said: "Allah knows best what they would have done."

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us; (H) and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bahram narrated to us: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us; (H) and Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us: Ma'qil—who is Ibn 'Ubaydillah—narrated to us, all of them from al-Zuhri, with the chain of transmission of Yunus and Ibn Abi Dhi'b, the like of their hadith, except that in the hadith of Shu'ayb and Ma'qil: "he was asked about the offspring of the polytheists."

Abu al-Tahir narrated to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Abi Dhi'b and Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ata' ibn Yazid, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was asked about the children of the polytheists, so he said: "Allah knows best what they would have done."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning al-Darawardi—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Every human being is born of his mother upon the fitrah (natural disposition), and then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian. If they are Muslims, then he is a Muslim. Every human being born of his mother is poked by Satan in his flanks, except Mary and her son."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—and he mentioned several hadiths, among which was that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever is born is born upon this fitrah (natural disposition), and then his parents make him a Jew and make him a Christian, just as you breed camels: do you find among them any born with its ear mutilated, until it is you who mutilate them?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think about one who dies young?" He said: "Allah knows best what they would have done."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us—both of them from al-A'mash, with this chain of transmission. In the hadith of Ibn Numayr: "There is no newborn born except upon the religion (al-millah)." And in the narration of Abu Bakr from Abu Mu'awiyah: "except upon this religion until his tongue expresses on his behalf." And in the narration of Abu Kurayb from Abu Mu'awiyah: "There is no newborn born except upon this fitrah until his tongue expresses on his behalf."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no newborn except that he is born upon the fitrah (natural disposition), and then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a polytheist." So a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if he died before that?" He said: "Allah knows best what they would have done."

Abu al-Tahir and Ahmad ibn 'Isa narrated to me, they said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed him that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no newborn except that he is born upon the fitrah (natural disposition)." Then he would say: Recite: {the natural disposition of Allah upon which He has created mankind; no change should there be in the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion.}
